newsitem.title: UK: MidEast Nov refinery shutdowns 450,000 bpd - IEA.
newsitem.headline: MidEast Nov refinery shutdowns 450,000 bpd - IEA.

text.p: Middle East Gulf oil refinery maintenance shutdowns are forecast to total 450,000 barrels per day (bpd) in November, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Friday.
In its end-October Monthly Oil Market Report, the Paris-based IEA said the bulk of this maintenance will be on export-oriented refineries.
The IEA also estimated Asia/Pacific maintenance shutdowns at 700,000 bpd in November, down from one million bpd in October.
But 490,000 bpd of new refining capacity in Korea will partly compensate the shutdowns, the IEA added.
The new capacity "is expected to start up and reach full capacity in a matter of weeks."
According to the IEA, U.S. refinery maintenance shutdowns are likely to be at their lowest levels for more than five years, although they should pick up sharply by January.
In Europe November maintenence is projected at 300,000 bpd, dropping to 130,000 in December and 100,000 in January 1997.
Refining margins generally fell during the first half of October in all major refining regions before recovering during the second half.
Margins for running sour crude in the Mediterranean were supported by firm gasoline and fuel oil prices which offset declining middle distillate values, the IEA said.
Refining margins in Rotterdam were underpinned by the stronger gasoline/crude differential which more than offset the narrowing gas oil/crude spread, it added.
On the U.S. Gulf coast margins rose largely due to firming gasoline and fuel oil relative to crude. The gas oil/crude differential in the region narrowed, but by less than in Europe.
Margins in Singapore running Dubai crude rose in line with strengthening gasoline and gas oil prices.
The margin for complex refineries rose by more than that for simple refineries, consistent with firming light product prices relative to fuel oil, the IEA said.
